# Catalog

Every plugin and skill in this repo. See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for how to install them.

## `essentials`

Everyday engineering skills that work in any agent, for commit messages, cross-tool session handoffs, grilling a plan before you act on it, sharpening a task to be deeper instead of bigger, and being tutored to mastery of a topic.

| Skill | Description |
|---|---|
| [`commit-message`](../plugins/essentials/skills/commit-message/SKILL.md) | Write a clear git commit message (Conventional Commits style) from the staged diff. Use when the user asks to commit, write or improve a commit message, or summarize staged changes for a commit. |
| [`grilling`](../plugins/essentials/skills/grilling/SKILL.md) | Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases. |
| [`handoff-notes`](../plugins/essentials/skills/handoff-notes/SKILL.md) | Write a concise handoff note so another agent session, another tool (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, pi, OpenCode), or a teammate can resume the current work without re-reading the conversation. Use when the user says hand off, wrap up, save progress, pause, switch tools, or before a context reset. |
| [`sharpen`](../plugins/essentials/skills/sharpen/SKILL.md) | Make a task deeper, not bigger, then rewrite the prompt. Use for /sharpen. |
| [`socratic-tutor`](../plugins/essentials/skills/socratic-tutor/SKILL.md) | Tutor the user to mastery of a topic by asking questions instead of lecturing, with a placement diagnostic, a skill map scored 0 to 5, spaced review and a final assessment. Use when the user asks to be tutored, quizzed or drilled, or to master a topic ("tutor me on X", "quiz me", "drill me", "help me master X"). Not for one-off "explain X" questions, and not for explaining code or a change (use teach). |

## `principles`

Twenty-four named engineering principles (prove it works, fix root causes, subtract before you add, build the lever, and more) that steer how agents design, build and verify, plus a benchmark checklist. One skill with one file per principle.

| Skill | Description |
|---|---|
| [`principles`](../plugins/principles/skills/principles/SKILL.md) | Named engineering principles (prove it works, fix root causes, subtract before you add, build the lever, and 20 more) that steer how an agent designs, builds and verifies. Use when a task or the user names a principle, when beau-mode tells you to apply one, or when deciding how much to build, where state and validation live, or what counts as proof. |

## `bstack`

Beau's rigorous agent workflow. beau-mode routes each task to a playbook and the principles; beau-help lists what the kit can do and what's new; waiting-on-me lists what waits on you across your repos; parallel-next finds the next planned work that won't collide with other sessions and starts the items you pick, each in its own beau-mode session; skills for understanding (how, why, teach, recall), debugging (root-cause finds a bug's cause from facts, not from reading the code), proof (verify-work, create- and maintain-verification-skill, create- and maintain-formal-verification-skill, swarm), design and planning (architect, arena, state-machines, technical-writing), product repos (scaffold-product and the Product phase playbook), review and trails (interrogate, show-me-your-work), closing out (debrief keeps a checked change record per PR and prints the brief and the release notes), improvement (reflect, correct, unslop, no-comments), and test economics (qualitydirector records per-test time and outcome, books the runs into the quality books, checks them and summarizes a week; local-ci runs a repo's CI on this machine and posts it to the PR as a commit status) do the steps. Adapted from Lauren Tan's pstack to work in any agent.

- `hooks/`: Claude `hooks.json`; Cursor `hooks/cursor.json`
- `agents/`: Claude Code, and Cursor via `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`

| Skill | Description |
|---|---|
| [`architect`](../plugins/bstack/skills/architect/SKILL.md) | Design before code. Ground in the affected systems, sketch types and signatures in at least two structurally different shapes (via arena), pick one, implement against it, and scrap it when friction shows the shape is wrong. Use for /architect, "design this", or work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape. |
| [`arena`](../plugins/bstack/skills/arena/SKILL.md) | Run N parallel candidates at the same task (ideally on different models), have a judge on another model score them against a rubric, pick a base, and graft the best parts of the others into it. Use for /arena, "arena this", "throw it in the arena", or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact (a design, an API, a doc, a tricky function) would lock in the wrong shape. |
| [`beau-help`](../plugins/bstack/skills/beau-help/SKILL.md) | List what agent-kit and bstack can do (skills, playbooks, subagents) and how to call each one, or show what changed since you last looked. Use for /beau-help, "what can you do", "which skill should I use for X", "what's new", or "what changed in bstack". |
| [`beau-mode`](../plugins/bstack/skills/beau-mode/SKILL.md) | Beau's way of doing engineering work with an agent. It picks a playbook, applies named principles, verifies on the real artifact, keeps a decision trail, and writes plain replies. Use for /beau-mode, "beau mode", or any non-trivial engineering task (a bug, a feature, a refactor, a perf problem, an investigation, a prototype, a skill edit, or an unattended run). Skip it for casual questions and one-line answers. |
| [`correct`](../plugins/bstack/skills/correct/SKILL.md) | Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible. Tries architecture first, then types, then a lint or CI check whose error names the fix, then a test, and docs last, and proves each new check fails on a real past mistake. Use for /correct, "agents keep doing X", or after correcting the same mistake twice. |
| [`create-formal-verification-skill`](../plugins/bstack/skills/create-formal-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | Generate a project-local verify-AREA skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits (model checker, prover, SMT-backed verifier). Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, "model-check this race", "prove this invariant", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers or unsafe code need more than tests. |
| [`create-verification-skill`](../plugins/bstack/skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | Generate a project-local verify-APP skill (for example verify-curator) that launches the real app, drives it like a user through a control CLI, captures evidence, and keeps a feature map. Any stack or surface. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a control skill for this repo", or when a project has no scripted way to prove behavior. |

Use for "how does X work", walkthroughs before a change, onboarding to unfamiliar code, and "where should this live" or "which layer owns this" questions. |
| [`interrogate`](../plugins/bstack/skills/interrogate/SKILL.md) | Adversarial multi-model review of a diff, branch, PR or design. Several adversaries try to break it, and a finding survives only when a run proves it. Use for "interrogate", "adversarial review", "tear this apart", "stress test this change", "find blind spots", or before shipping a contested or risky change. |
| [`local-ci`](../plugins/bstack/skills/local-ci/SKILL.md) | Run a repo's CI on this machine instead of GitHub-hosted runners and report the result on the PR as the `local-ci` commit status, and run a local fallback for a job GitHub didn't start. Use to move a private repo's CI off Actions minutes, to set up or check the launchd agent that runs it, when a PR's `local-ci` status is missing, pending or red, when an Actions job failed without starting (spending limit, outage), or for "run CI locally", "post local-ci", "why is local-ci red". |

Use for /maintain-formal-verification-skill, "is the model still true to the code", or after merges and refactors that touched verified code without rechecking it. |
| [`maintain-verification-skill`](../plugins/bstack/skills/maintain-verification-skill/SKILL.md) | Periodic pass that keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest. ## `cfo`

A CFO for AI and cloud spending. Keeps a private cost ledger from receipts and provider billing data, separates cash cost from API-equivalent cost, estimates runs before they start, writes a weekly brief, and proposes budgets and cuts for you to approve. Never pays, cancels or deletes anything itself.

| Skill | Description |
|---|---|
| [`cfo-books`](../plugins/cfo/skills/cfo-books/SKILL.md) | Check, append to and summarize the CFO's private books (ledger, projects, budgets, renewals, questions). Checks find schema errors, forbidden content such as card numbers, account IDs and API keys, and rewritten ledger history. Use before committing or opening a PR against the books, to add ledger rows, to get a month's spend numbers, when a books CI check fails, or when asked to "check the books", "validate the ledger" or "summarize the month". |
| [`cfo-brief`](../plugins/cfo/skills/cfo-brief/SKILL.md) | The CFO's weekly routine. Collects new receipts, invoices, vendor notices and billing data into the private books, checks spend against the budget, finds waste and renewals, writes a brief, and sends it with decisions and questions for the user to approve. Proposes; never acts. Use for "CFO brief", "weekly finance review", "check my spending this week", or from a weekly scheduled task. |
| [`estimate-run`](../plugins/cfo/skills/estimate-run/SKILL.md) | Estimate what an agent run, a charter or a whole project will cost before it starts, in both cash and API-equivalent terms, with a typical and a high figure based on past runs where the books have them. Fills a run charter's estimate and budget. Use for "what will this cost", "estimate this run", "price this charter", "is this worth running", or when writing a run charter. |
| [`spend-snapshot`](../plugins/cfo/skills/spend-snapshot/SKILL.md) | Answer "what am I spending" on AI, cloud and developer tools, by provider and by project, with month-to-date spend against the budget, renewals coming up, and anything unknown. Reads the private books plus receipts and billing data from connected tools. Use for "what am I spending", "how much do my AI tools cost", "am I over budget", "spend snapshot", or before deciding on a new tool or plan. |
